author: Tony Liebert
title: Quinn Hughes delivers OT winner to keep Team USA's Olympic hopes alive - NewsBreak
text:
By Tony Liebert ,
8 hours ago Superstar Wild defenseman Quinn Hughes continues to prove that he is one of the best hockey players in the world at the Olympics. He delivered an OT winner against Sweden on Wednesday to send Team USA to the semifinals.
There were four Minnesota Wild players on the ice during Wednesday's quarterfinal game between Sweden and Team USA. It was a defensive effort for much of the game, while Hughes and Brock Faber were two of the most impactful players on the ice.
Hughes and his brother, Jack Hughes, assisted a Dylan Larkin goal in the second period to give the U.S. its first lead of the game. It marked the fourth straight game in which Quinn has secured a point in the box score. Hughes and Auston Matthews are the only players on Team USA to score a point in every game this Olympics.
Faber, Hughes, and Matt Boldy weren't the only players from the Wild on the ice on Wednesday. Joel Eriksson Ek represented Sweden, while Marcus Johansson, Filip Gustavsson, and Jesper Wallstedt did not dress for their home country.
Sweden scored a goal with just over 90 seconds left in regulation to force overtime, but Hughes found the back of the net for a game-winner. He was assisted by Matthews and Boldy.
Team USA will now face Slovakia in Friday's semifinal round. Canada will face Finland on the other side of the bracket. The gold medal game will be on Sunday.
